mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months signals central bank easing, which lowers discount rates and increases present-value pricing of future equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% triggers a risk-off reaction in equity markets, compressing forward discount rates and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 150,000 jobs signals a labor market recovery, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in recovery periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% triggers a risk-on equity premium as investors anticipate sustained job growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in low-unemployment periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
